subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should OpenClaw make common shell-shaped allowlist matches such as tilde-expanded script paths enforceable and auto-executable, or keep them prompt-only and document the limitation?
rationale: The current behavior conflicts with the on-miss docs and breaks production automation, but the gate exists to prevent auto-executing a shell command whose resolved execution cannot be safely pinned.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
options.body: Teach the POSIX authorization renderer to bind safe common shapes such as tilde-expanded local paths, keep unsafe shell expansion prompt-only, and add Darwin/source regression coverage plus docs for remaining limitations.

options.title: Document prompt-only limitation
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior and update docs/warnings so operators know shell-shaped Darwin commands must be rewritten as argv-clean absolute paths or explicitly approved.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell commands
options.body: Permit matched Darwin allowlist commands to run without an enforced plan, accepting a broader shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
recommendation.body: Teach the POSIX authorization renderer to bind safe common shapes such as tilde-expanded local paths, keep unsafe shell expansion prompt-only, and add Darwin/source regression coverage plus docs for remaining limitations.

likelyOwner.reason: The current gate and recent approval-regression history are concentrated in Vincent Koc’s exec approval work.
